title: Carry Credit on Storage Days for Grain Committed to the Cooperative
content:
Grain the member has sold to the cooperative earns a carry credit against the days billed on a storage agreement, because the cooperative carries part of the storage on grain committed to it. This credit applies to Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements and is decided from the member's position under Grain Marketing Contracts.

## Rule

Where twenty thousand bushels or more have been settled on the member's grain marketing contracts in the last twelve months and the member holds an active marketing contract for the same commodity with bushels still open, the days billed are halved and any part of a day carried to the next whole day.

Where five thousand bushels or more have been settled in the last twelve months, or the member holds an active marketing contract for the same commodity with bushels still open, the days billed are three quarters of the days counted and any part of a day carried to the next whole day.

And otherwise every day counted is billed.

## The two records the credit is read from

The first is the bushels settled on the member's contracts under Grain Marketing Contracts over the last twelve months, taken from the settlement entries in that product's ledger. The second is whether an active marketing contract for the same commodity still carries open bushels.

| Bushels settled in the last twelve months | An active contract for the same commodity with bushels still open | Days billed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20000 or more | yes | half the days counted, any part of a day carried up to the next whole day |
| 20000 or more | no | three quarters of the days counted, any part of a day carried up |
| 5000 or more but under 20000 | yes or no | three quarters of the days counted, any part of a day carried up |
| under 5000 | yes | three quarters of the days counted, any part of a day carried up |
| under 5000 | no | every day counted is billed |

## Worked credits, on hypothetical figures

**Twenty-five days counted, 26000 bushels settled over the twelve months, an open contract for the same commodity.** Half of twenty-five is twelve and a half; the part day is carried up, so 13 days are billed.

**Twenty-five days counted, 9000 bushels settled, no contract still open.** Three quarters of twenty-five is eighteen and three quarters; carried up, 19 days are billed.

**Thirty days counted, 1200 bushels settled, no contract still open.** Neither threshold is reached, so all 30 days counted are billed.

## Boundary readings

Twenty thousand bushels exactly, with an open contract for the same commodity, reaches the higher credit, the threshold being twenty thousand bushels or more. Nineteen thousand nine hundred with an open contract falls to the second line, the open contract alone carrying it there. Five thousand bushels exactly reaches the second line without any open contract at all.
